title: Down material: what are you getting for it?
outcomes: Counts material first, pawns and pieces for both sides
Labels a position where a side has given up material sound or practical using the engine at depth 16, and says it is evidence, not proof
Recognises a position where nothing was given up

steps.text:
A **gambit** gives up a pawn or more. It can be sound if it buys **compensation**: something durable such as a lead in development, open lines toward the king, a safer king or the initiative.
Name what you got, and how long it lasts. In this course 'sound' means the engine at depth 16 rates the side within half a pawn of level; 'practical chances only' means more than half a pawn behind but less than three; anything worse is simply bad.

steps.caption: Black to move. White is two pawns down (6 pawns against 8) and has castled; White gave one pawn on move four and another on move six.

line.say: Black develops the knight. The king is still on e8 and the bishop on c8 has not moved.
cxd4 wins a pawn back. The b- and c-files are now half-open for White's rooks.
Black strikes in the centre at once. If White cannot keep the files open and the centre alive, the compensation fades.
exd5 takes it. White's compensation is the centre and open b- and c-files, not a lead in development: Nb1 and Bc1 have not moved. Engine, depth 16: about level.

steps.text:
**Compensation runs on a clock.** A lead in development shrinks each time the opponent develops a piece or castles. Count the moves the opponent still needs to catch up, and ask whether you can make threats faster than that.
The next board shows a different gambit, also a pawn down, after slow moves by White.

steps.caption: White to move. White is a pawn down in a different gambit, after slow moves by White and normal development by Black.

line.say: The bishop retreats. Black has castled; the king is no longer in the centre.
Black gains space on the queenside.
White develops the queen, but the lead in development is gone.

claims.statement: The engine at depth 16 rates White more than half a pawn behind.
White has two pawns on the queenside.
White has four pawns on the kingside.
Black has three pawns on the queenside.
Black has four pawns on the kingside.
The black king has castled to g8.

steps.text:
**When it holds.** The compensation is real if what you gave buys something that outlasts the opponent's next few moves. **It fails** when lines are closed, when the opponent has already developed, or when the engine rates you more than half a pawn behind.
**Rule of thumb:** give material back only for something tangible. The engine verdict is evidence at one depth, not proof.

steps.title: Down material, different verdicts
steps.prompt: Count the material first: pawns and pieces for both sides. Decide whether the side that gave material has sound compensation, practical chances only, or nothing was given up. Predict, then check.
Pick one silent item. How sure were you before the answer, and what did you count first: pawns, pieces, or the engine number? Write both.
